{"sourceType":"ESA Tender Action","sourceSystem":"ESA esa-star Publication","sourcePage":"https://esastar-publication-ext.sso.esa.int/ESATenderActions/filter/open","id":161043,"idEra":23678,"activityNumber":"1000043899","contractNumber":"","tanumber":"1-12966","title":"TIME DIVISION DUPLEXING (TDD) KA-BAND IN-ORBIT EXPERIMENT FOR NGSO 5G BROADBAND SERVICES (ARTES 4.0 SPL 5G/6G 3E.029)","description":"The objective of the activity is to develop and perform an in-orbit experiment of Non-GeoSynchornous Orbit (NGSO) payload technology to prove the feasibility of Time Division Duplexing method in Ka-band for broadband services, allowing operators to gain access to 3 GHz of additional Ka-band spectrum (24.5 - 27.5 GHz) via 5G New Radio waveform in Frequency Range 2 (FR2).Targeted Improvements:Access to an additional 3 GHz of terrestrial spectrum between 24.5-27.5GHz. 30% improvement in spectrum efficiency due to Time Division Duplexing optimisation.Description: The use of Time Domain Duplexing (TDD) for satellite communications can provide access to an additional 3 GHz of Ka-band spectrum (24.5 - 27.5 GHz) via 5G New Radio waveform in Frequency Range 2 (FR 2). The feasibility of employing this technology in Non-Geosynchronous Orbit (NGSO) broadband systems depends on the round-trip time as well as on the waveform and system operations (e.g., synchronisation), which necessitate in-orbit tests to confirm feasibility. TDD technology is highly latency dependent, and there exists a number of technical challenges to be addressed in-orbit:- ability to synchronise uplink with downlink on the satellite payload as well as the user terminal- varying guard times that are required under various geometrical configurations- timing reference accuracy required by the payload- frequency of ephemeris update rate required at the terminal- RF front-end performance given the Tx/Rx co-existence- ability of the ground segment to schedule various uplink/downlink capacity allocations (from e.g. 90/10 down- to up-link ratio to 50/50 down- to up-link ratio). The activity shall therefore develop a scaled Ka-band payload engineering model, employing the 5G New Radio waveform and shall confirm the feasibility of TDD in Ka-band systems in real operating conditions by testing the payload in-orbit. The payload shall be embarked on a NGSO hosted payload service, for a period of at least 4 months, in order to test it under a variety of operating conditions (e.g., different elevations) and 5G New Radio waveform configurations (e.g., different guard time intervals).
